title: Let's Ask Gauss: Improved One-Run Privacy Auditing
abstract: arXiv:2606.12733v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Privacy auditing provides an important safeguard by estimating the actual information leaked by a model, thus ensuring that theoretical privacy guarantees hold in practice. We study empirical privacy auditing for differentially private (DP) machine learning, focusing on efficient one-run methods for mechanisms such as DP-SGD. Prior one-run approaches threshold training examples or "canaries" into binary membership guesses, which discards useful information. We show that, in the white-box DP-SGD setting, canary-aligned signals naturally form a sequence of random variables whose normalized sum is asymptotically Gaussian. We show that this gaussian perspective can also be naturally extended to other composition mechanisms that satisfy a classical, triangular-array, or martingale central limit theorem. Leveraging this distributional perspective, we develop a DP-auditing framework that leads to tighter privacy lower bounds from a single t

translated_title: 让我们请教高斯：改进的单次运行隐私审计
translated_abstract: 隐私审计通过估计模型实际泄露的信息量，提供了一项重要的安全保障，从而确保理论上的隐私保证在实践中真正成立。我们研究了差分隐私（DP）机器学习的经验性隐私审计，重点针对DP-SGD等机制的高效单次运行方法。以往的单次运行方法将训练样本或“金丝雀”阈值化为二元成员身份猜测，这丢弃了有用的信息。我们证明，在白盒DP-SGD设置中，与金丝雀对齐的信号自然形成一个随机变量序列，其归一化之和是渐近高斯的。我们还表明，这一高斯视角可以自然地扩展到其他满足经典、三角阵列或鞅中心极限定理的组合机制。利用这一分布视角，我们开发了一个差分隐私审计框架，能够仅通过单次训练就获得更紧的隐私下界。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于中心极限定理的高斯分布视角的单次运行差分隐私审计框架，将金丝雀对齐信号视为随机变量序列而非二值化猜测，从而从单次训练中就能获得更紧的隐私下界。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a one-run DP auditing framework that leverages a Gaussian distributional perspective (via central limit theorems) on canary-aligned signals instead of binarizing them, yielding tighter privacy lower bounds from a single training run.
